Area.evidence_source: All participants suggested that their suicidal experience made them realise the importance of communicating their emotional distress. This required them to challenge masculine stereotypes of being unemotional and reluctant to seek help. Three participants said that their mothers or girlfriends were pivotal in the process of opening up about their emotions. In the aftermath of his suicide attempt Johan came to the realisation: The reason you are going through such a tough time is because you are not sharing your problems with anyone else. … When I have a fall-out like this and I feel stressed I will immediately start talking to my parents, because then you know I can prevent it and then I don't have to feel that shame. Two participants also commented that talking to a psychologist or psychiatrist helped them to understand their experience of attempting suicide. Talking also enabled them to develop a different perspective of themselves and their lives. Revealing that they were suicidal to psychologists, psychiatrists and family members was considered to be crucial by participants in becoming more self-assertive and overcoming suicidal behaviour.
